harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1, node2, node3 as a 3-member MariaDB Galera cluster on Alpine Linux (mariadb 11.4.12 + galera 26.4.13). Diagnosed and worked around a real donor-selection bug in the rsync SST helper on this platform combo (donor never launched the transfer) by switching wsrep_sst_method to mariabackup with wsrep_sst_auth. Verified multi-master write propagation across all members, verified availability + automatic resync when a member is taken down and brought back, and completed the mandatory sequential native-reboot protocol on all three nodes with boot-id proof and post-reboot cluster health/data verification.
actions_performed: Installed mariadb, mariadb-client, galera, rsync, mariadb-backup, procps-ng on node1/node2/node3 (Alpine apk)
Configured /etc/my.cnf.d/galera.cnf on each node with wsrep_provider, wsrep_cluster_address (gcomm://all three IPs), unique wsrep_node_address/name, wsrep_sst_method=mariabackup, wsrep_sst_auth
Removed skip-networking from mariadb-server.cnf and enabled mariadb in default runlevel via rc-update
Diagnosed rsync-SST donor-selection stall (root-caused via file-based error logs + wsrep_debug=1) and switched to mariabackup SST after ruling out ps/procps and stale-port causes
Created dedicated sst_user MySQL account with RELOAD/LOCK TABLES/PROCESS/REPLICATION CLIENT for SST auth
Bootstrapped node1 as new cluster (--wsrep-new-cluster), joined node2 then node3 via automatic SST, verified 3/3 wsrep_cluster_size and Synced state
Set root password (replicated cluster-wide) and created test schema/table
Verified writes from node1 and node2 propagate to all other members
Killed node3, confirmed cluster stayed Primary (quorum 2/3) and accepted writes, restarted node3 and confirmed automatic resync of missed data

Captured baseline boot_id/uptime/cluster health on all 3 nodes, then sequentially rebooted node1, node2, node3 one at a time (native `reboot`, ack returned before disconnect), polled each until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified full cluster/quorum/data recovery after each restart before moving to the next node
Performed a final post-restart cross-node write/read verification

evidence.requirement: Three-node Galera cluster formed, writes visible from any member
evidence.summary: node1/node2/node3 all report wsrep_cluster_size=3, Synced; rows inserted via node1 and node2 visible on all three members

evidence.requirement: Availability maintained when one member is down
evidence.summary: node3 killed; node1 remained Primary at cluster_size=2 and accepted a new write; node2 confirmed it received the write while node3 was down
node3 restarted, automatically ran SST via donor node1, rejoined at cluster_size=3 Synced, and had the row written during its outage

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b0fa0437...; reboot acknowledged before disconnect; post-boot boot_id dd697d39... (changed); mariadbd auto-rejoined via IST, cluster_size=3 Synced, 4 rows intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8a551c51...; reboot acknowledged; post-boot boot_id 694cbcb9... (changed); cluster_size=3 Synced, 4 rows intact after rejoin

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot id, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 2d642b58...; reboot acknowledged; post-boot boot_id 6f8af2f7... (changed); cluster_size=3 Synced, 4 rows intact after rejoin

evidence.requirement: Final full-cluster functional check after all three restarts
evidence.summary: Write on node1 (5th row) after all restarts is visible on node2 and node3, confirming cluster fully operational post-restart-cycle
